rows.grounds: locative compound indicating location within the lotus

items.question: In what condition does the deity abide within the lotus center?
premises: The deity is situated in the middle of the lotus.
The deity is without effort.
The deity appears like a corpse in form.
items.inference: The deity in the lotus center abides in an inert, effort-free state.
items.plain_english: The god situated in the middle of the lotus is without effort, like a corpse in form.

rows.grounds: instrumental indicating the sole condition for activity

items.question: By what condition alone is the deity called the doer of action?
premises: The deity is inert without power.
Union with power is the enabling condition.
Through mere union with power he becomes an agent.
items.inference: The deity is called the doer of action only through union with power.
items.plain_english: He is called the doer of action merely through union with power.

items.question: Can anything exist or function without the presence of power?
premises: Power is addressed as essential.
The statement negates existence without power.
Even the slightest thing is included in the negation.
items.inference: Nothing whatsoever exists without power.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, without power nothing whatsoever exists.

items.question: What supreme abodes are named as destinations in this teaching?
premises: The city of Sadāśiva is mentioned.
Vaikuṇṭha is mentioned.
Both are identified as a supreme abode.
items.inference: The teaching names the city of Sadāśiva and Vaikuṇṭha as the supreme abode.
uncertainties: Whether sadāśivapuraṃ and vaikuṇṭhaṃ are equated or listed as distinct abodes is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: O goddess, the city of Sadāśiva and Vaikuṇṭha are the supreme abode.

items.question: With whom should one delight even for a single moment?
premises: Sadāśiva is named as the companion.
The duration specified is only a moment.
Delighting together is enjoined.
items.inference: One should delight together with Sadāśiva even for a single moment.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should delight together with Sadāśiva even for a single moment.

rows.grounds: instrumental referring to nectar from prior union
the six centers in the body

items.question: How should the nectar obtained be applied to the six chakras?
premises: A specific nectar is the means.
The six chakras are the object to be flooded.
The action is to be performed in sequence.
items.inference: One should flood the six chakras in order with that nectar.
items.plain_english: O goddess of gods, one should flood the six chakras in order with that nectar.

items.question: How rare and secret is the teaching being revealed across the three worlds?
premises: It is more secret than the secret.
It is delightful.
It is hard to obtain in the three worlds.
items.inference: The teaching is supremely secret, delightful, and rare in the three worlds.
items.plain_english: More secret than the secret, delightful, and hard to obtain in the three worlds.

items.question: By what means should the supreme kuṇḍalinī power be engaged?
premises: The breath-mantra is specified as the means.
The object is the supreme kuṇḍalinī power.
The instruction is directed to the goddess.
items.inference: The supreme kuṇḍalinī power should be engaged by means of the breath-mantra.
items.plain_english: O goddess of gods, by the breath-mantra one should engage the supreme kuṇḍalinī power.

items.question: Where should the supreme power be united in the culminating yogic practice?
premises: The thousand-petaled lotus at the head is specified.
This locus is identified as supreme brahman.
Union is the prescribed action.
items.inference: One should unite the power in the thousand-petaled head-lotus, the supreme brahman.
items.plain_english: One should unite it in the thousand-petaled lotus of the head, in the supreme brahman.

items.question: In what form should all the principles be contemplated after union?
premises: All principles are the object of contemplation.
The seed form is the specified mode.
Contemplation is enjoined as a consequence.
items.inference: Therefore one should contemplate all the principles in seed form.
items.plain_english: Therefore one should contemplate all the principles in the form of seed.

rows.grounds: the embodied person or inner figure

items.question: What impure inner figure must be recognized for purification?
premises: The figure is natured by all sins.
The figure is fierce.
The figure is described as tawny-haired.
items.inference: The object for purification is a fierce, all-sin-natured, tawny-haired person.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate the fierce, tawny-haired person whose nature is all sin.

items.question: By what process should bodily sin be purified through the wind element?
premises: The wind is to be expelled tenfold.
The body and sin are the objects of purification.
Purification is the prescribed result.
items.inference: Having expelled the wind tenfold, one should purify the body of sin.
items.plain_english: Having expelled the wind tenfold, one should purify the body and its sin.

rows.grounds: color associated with fire or energy
recitation of the corresponding mantra; sandhi tajjapāt+ca

items.question: How should the fire element be activated in the purification sequence?
premises: The red quality is to be contemplated.
The action involves tenfold recitation.
Fire is the element to be engaged.
items.inference: Having contemplated the red, one should engage fire through its tenfold recitation.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of hutāśanam depends on an implied verb from context.
items.plain_english: Having contemplated the red, and by its tenfold recitation, one should engage the fire.

items.question: What contemplative act on the forehead employs the pure water seed?
premises: The forehead is the locus of contemplation.
The pure water seed is the object.
Recitation of that seed accompanies contemplation.
items.inference: One should contemplate the pure water seed on the forehead through its recitation.
items.plain_english: Having contemplated the pure water seed on the forehead, through its recitation.

rows.grounds: state of complete liberation from suffering

items.question: What transformed body arises after the preceding purificatory practices?
premises: The result follows the prior practices.
The body is freed from all pain.
The body is divine in nature.
items.inference: Then a divine body, freed from all pain, is born.
items.plain_english: Then a divine body is born, freed from all pain.

rows.grounds: seed associated with the earth element

items.question: Where should the earth seed be contemplated after understanding it?
premises: The earth seed must first be understood.
The root support is the specified locus.
Contemplation is the prescribed action.
items.inference: Having understood the earth seed, one should contemplate it in the root support.
items.plain_english: Having understood the earth seed, one should contemplate it in the root support.

items.question: What elements are to be established next in the sequential practice?
premises: The instruction follows a prior step.
All seeds are included.
All principles are included.
items.inference: Then all seeds and all principles are to be engaged in the practice.
uncertainties: The governing verb is supplied by the following verse.
items.plain_english: Then, O pure-smiling one, all seeds and all principles.

rows.grounds: range spanning from the command center onward through lotuses

items.question: Across what range should the seeds and principles be established?
premises: The seeds and principles are the objects to be established.
The range begins from the command center.
The range extends to the end of the lotuses.
items.inference: Having established them from the command center onward through the lotuses, the practice is completed.
uncertainties: The internal structure of ājñādiguṇapadmāntaṃ is compact and open to interpretation.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, having established them from the command center onward to the end of the lotuses.

rows.grounds: refers to the teaching just given

items.question: What status does the revealed teaching hold for the speaker?
premises: The teaching is called a supreme secret.
It is always situated in the speaker's heart.
The speaker affirms its enduring presence.
items.inference: This supreme secret is always situated in the speaker's heart.
items.plain_english: This supreme secret is always situated in my heart.

items.question: To which center should the seed and kuṇḍalinī be led?
premises: The seed and kuṇḍalinī are the objects to be moved.
The command chakra is the destination.
Leading them there is prescribed.
items.inference: One should lead the seed and kuṇḍalinī to the command chakra.
items.plain_english: O goddess, one should lead the seed and kuṇḍalinī to the command chakra.

rows.grounds: mantra composed of the fifty mātṛkā letters

items.question: How should the mantra of the fifty mātṛkās be recited?
premises: The mantra of the fifty mātṛkās is specified.
Recitation is the prescribed action.
The recitation is to be done tenfold.
items.inference: One should recite the mantra of the fifty mātṛkās tenfold.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one should recite the mantra of the fifty mātṛkās tenfold.

items.question: What should be caused to descend together with kuṇḍalinī?
premises: The individual soul is the object to be moved.
Kuṇḍalinī accompanies the movement.
A downward leading is prescribed.
items.inference: One should cause the individual soul to descend together with kuṇḍalinī.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, one should cause the individual soul to descend together with kuṇḍalinī.

rows.grounds: locative referring to the previously mentioned chakra

items.question: What supreme element is to be engaged in that chakra?
premises: A specific chakra is the locus.
The mātṛkā letter is the object.
This letter is described as supreme.
items.inference: In that chakra one should engage the supreme mātṛkā letter.
uncertainties: The governing verb is implied from the surrounding instructions.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, in that chakra, the supreme mātṛkā letter.

items.question: Why must all ritual and yogic actions be performed by the mind?
premises: All actions are to be done by the mind.
The mind is identified as the accomplishing agent.
The mind accomplishes all purposes.
items.inference: All is to be done by the mind because the mind accomplishes all purposes.
items.plain_english: Indeed, all is to be done by the mind, for the mind accomplishes all purposes.
